title: Weights acceptance, transform, and serve-readiness pipeline
creator: Asha Patel
description: Create an end-to-end pipeline that validates external open-source model weights on intake, deterministically converts them into runtime artifacts (quantized and fused variants), attaches provenance metadata, runs a standardized smoke and safety suite, and publishes a first-pass performance profile and pin candidate for downstream serving and rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Weights dropped into intake bucket trigger automated fingerprinting and schema validation (hash, declared architecture, and declared tokenizer).
Conversion produces deterministic artifacts (float32 reference, 8-bit quantized, 4-bit quantized where supported) with repeatable checksums and a conversion log attached to the artifact metadata.
Automated smoke tests (correct tokenization, single-batch generation for 16/64 tokens) pass against the converted artifacts without runtime crashes on target CUDA and ROCm CI runners.
A safety/regression harness runs prompt-suite and flags regressions in safety categories (toxicity, hallucination heuristics) with clear triage steps for failures.

Performance profiler publishes median latency, p95, and cost estimate per 1k tokens to the model catalog and marks a pin-candidate (semantic version + content hash) so Console rollouts can reference it.
Provenance metadata (source URL, original hash, conversion toolchain version, converter-config, and responsible engineer) is embedded in the artifact manifest and surfaced in the onboarding UI.
Automatic canary gating: model cannot be published to the public catalog unless canary validations (on small subset of Dedicated pool) succeed and a reviewer signs off.
Documentation with conversion cookbook and troubleshooting runbook published on Confluence and linked in the ticket.
technical_notes: Use the artifact-gateway lambda to perform initial antivirus and file-size checks before handing to conversion cluster.
Conversion pipeline should be idempotent: given same input and converter-config it must produce identical binary blobs and identical metadata checksums.
Support conversion outputs: ONNX for CPU fallback, Triton/TS for GPU runtime, and optimized fused operator binaries for our runtime where applicable.
Quantization targets: q8_dynamic for broad hardware, q4x for experiments — include calibration dataset snapshots in artifact store to allow repro runs.
Integrate with perf-runner: run 3 warmup runs + 20 measured runs; capture token-per-second, memory highwater, and KV cache behavior for long-context tests.
Safety suite will include a mixture of internal prompts and community-sourced prompts; failures produce structured issue templates for research review.
Embed conversion logs and runtime trace snippets into the artifact manifest; store the full logs in S3 with lifecycle rule (90 days hot, 1 year archive).
